description: Realtime surfacing for project inbox items — emit a project-scoped 'inbox item persisted' hint strictly after persistence, deliver it with strict server-side project isolation over the existing MohistHub/EventBridge path, and consume it on the Web as invalidation-only (live unread count, live inbox list refresh, high-attention in-app notice with duplicate suppression).

tasks.title: Server emits project-scoped realtime hint after non-duplicate inbox item persistence
tasks.description: Add `com.mohist.inbox.item-persisted` to `EventCatalog.ReverseDns`. In `InboxProjectionHandler.ProjectAsync`, capture the `InboxInsertResult` from `InsertAsync` and, when `!result.AlreadyExisted`, publish the hint via `IEventPublisher.PublishAsync` with `extensions["projectid"] = draft.ProjectId` and an identity-only payload `{ itemId, projectId, kind, issueId, issueNumber }`. The publish is awaited inline after the successful insert and inside the existing try/catch so a publish failure cannot corrupt the source-event projection. Delivery reuses the existing bus → EventBridge → per-connection fanout (no new SignalR method).
acceptanceCriteria: Exactly one project-scoped realtime hint is emitted after a new (non-duplicate) inbox item is durably persisted (unit/integration test).
No hint is emitted when an insert is deduplicated and no new inbox item is created (test asserts AlreadyExisted path publishes nothing).
No hint is emitted before persistence succeeds; a failed insert produces no hint (test).
Hint payload carries only identity (itemId, projectId, kind, issueId, issueNumber) and no complete inbox state (test).
Hint carries `extensions["projectid"]` so the dispatcher can route it (test).
A hint-publish exception is swallowed/logged and does not break the source-event projection (test).
`npm test` (server) passes with TreatWarningsAsErrors.
tasks.output: EventCatalog entry + InboxProjectionHandler hint emission + server tests
tasks.notes: Reuses EventBridge fanout (D2). No new SignalR method, no groups. Bus re-entrancy is tolerated; keep publish after the DB insert inside the existing try/catch.

tasks.title: Server-side project isolation for realtime delivery via per-connection affinity and a gated dispatcher filter
tasks.description: Add a per-connection `projectId` (default null) to `ConnectionSubscriptionRegistry` and read `Context.GetHttpContext()?.Request.Query["projectId"]` (already sent by `events-hub.ts`) in `MohistHub.OnConnectedAsync`. Add a generalized, backward-compatible project filter to `UserNotificationDispatcher.ResolveTargetConnectionsAsync`: when the event carries `extensions["projectid"]` AND the connection has declared a project, include the connection only on project match; when either side is absent, behavior is unchanged (type-only match). This is the only genuinely new server mechanism and is generalized per the dispatcher's documented extension point.
acceptanceCriteria: A project-A session receives inbox hints for project-A items and never receives hints for project-B items (no cross-project leakage) (integration test).
Hint is delivered only to sessions subscribed to the owning project over the existing per-connection subscription path (test).
Events WITHOUT `extensions["projectid"]` still reach project-affinitized connections byte-for-byte unchanged (regression test).
A connection that did not declare a projectId keeps type-only matching behavior (test).
No new multi-user routing, groups, or new SignalR methods are introduced (verify via diff).
`npm test` (server) passes with TreatWarningsAsErrors.
tasks.output: ConnectionSubscriptionRegistry projectId + MohistHub affinity capture + UserNotificationDispatcher gated filter + server tests
tasks.notes: Project affinity is transport-level presentation state, intentionally not durable (matches project-inbox spec). The filter is gated on both sides so every existing non-projectid event is unchanged — this is the key blast-radius risk, covered by the regression test.

tasks.title: Web subscribes to inbox hint via the central dispatcher and invalidates the inbox query (invalidation-only)
tasks.description: Add the inbox hint type to `REVERSE_DNS_EVENT_TYPES` / `EVENT_TYPES` (`canonical-event-types.ts`). Handle it inside `LiveTaskProvider.handleEvent` (the existing central event switch) via a small inbox-effects module that invalidates the shared TanStack Query key `['inbox', projectId]`. Remove `useInboxLiveRefresh` and its second SignalR connection so the app runs a single events connection. The Web never synthesizes an InboxItem from the hint; it only triggers a refetch of the authoritative inbox HTTP API.
acceptanceCriteria: On hint receipt, `['inbox', projectId]` is invalidated and the inbox HTTP API is re-queried (test).
The Web does not synthesize or persist an InboxItem from the hint payload; the hint is treated as invalidation only (test).
The inbox page inserts/refreshes the affected item without a full browser navigation/page reload on a hint for the current project (test).
The inbox page does not refresh on a hint for a different project (test).
Reconnect or a dropped hint recovers truth via the next inbox query; no inbox data is lost (test).
`useInboxLiveRefresh` and its second SignalR connection are removed; all former callers are covered by the central dispatcher path (verify by grep — no remaining references).
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes.
tasks.output: canonical-event-types entry + LiveTaskProvider inbox-effects handling + removal of useInboxLiveRefresh + web tests
tasks.notes: Single-connection decision (D5). The shared `['inbox', projectId]` key drives both the inbox page and the app-shell unread count, so one invalidation updates both surfaces.

tasks.title: App shell surfaces a live project inbox unread count
tasks.description: Add a `useUnreadInboxCount(projectId)` selector that derives the unread count client-side from the shared cached `['inbox', projectId]` list query (`list.filter(i => !i.isRead).length`). Surface the count in the app shell / project navigation. Because the count reads the same query key invalidated by T-003, it updates live as items arrive or are marked read without a manual refresh and without any new HTTP endpoint (no API contract changes).
acceptanceCriteria: Unread count updates live (without manual refresh) when a new item arrives for the current project (test drives a hint → invalidation → refetch → count change).
Unread count updates live when an inbox item is marked read (test).
Displayed count reflects only the current project's unread items and never includes another project's items (test).
No new HTTP endpoint or API contract change is introduced (the count is derived from the existing inbox list query) (verify by diff).
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes.
tasks.output: useUnreadInboxCount selector + app shell unread count rendering + web tests
tasks.notes: D6. Inbox is a bounded, low-volume operator feed, so refetching the list per hint is acceptable. Revisit with a count endpoint only if volume grows (would require relaxing the no-API-changes rule in a separate change).

tasks.title: High-attention in-app notice with duplicate-notice suppression
tasks.description: For `workflow_failed` and `approval_requested` hints, render a lightweight in-app (toast/inline) notice carrying the relevant issue context (number + kind). Evaluate suppression against the current route at hint time: suppress when the user is viewing the referred issue (`/projects/:p/issues/:n` with matching number) or is on the inbox page (`/projects/:p/inbox`); otherwise fire the notice once for that hint. `issue_started` / `issue_completed` are not high-attention and do not toast. Suppression uses the hint payload's `issueNumber` and the router's current location — no extra server round-trip.
acceptanceCriteria: A `workflow_failed` hint shows an in-app notice surfacing the relevant issue context (test).
An `approval_requested` hint shows an in-app notice surfacing the relevant issue context (test).
The notice is in-app only: no browser push, mobile push, email, desktop notification, sound, or OS notification permission prompt (verify by diff + test).
Notice is suppressed when the user is currently viewing the same issue the item refers to (test).
Notice is suppressed when the user is on the inbox page for that project (the item appears live there) (test).
Notice fires when the user is viewing an unrelated issue or an unrelated part of the app (test).
`issue_started` and `issue_completed` hints do not show a notice (test).
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes.
tasks.output: In-app notice component + route-based suppression logic in the inbox-effects module + web tests
tasks.notes: D7. Suppression is route-based (the inbox page has no per-item detail view today); if a per-item detail view is added later, narrow the suppression check to the focused itemId.
